title: Sunflower shoot variety selection
subtitle: What type of sunflower seed to buy for microgreen growing, and what to avoid
excerpt: Variety selection for sunflower shoots is less about choosing between named cultivars and more about getting the seed type right: unhulled (in-shell) sunflower seed that is untreated and intended for growing or sprouting. Most large-seed sunflower varieties work; the key is the presence of the outer hull.
sourceNotes: UMass Extension microgreens guides (open-access). Cornell Cooperative Extension indoor growing material. Sunflower shoot seed selection guidance synthesised from extension service material and established microgreen grower practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: Sunflower seed with the outer hull (the striped black-and-white shell) intact. This is the seed type needed for microgreen growing. The hull protects the embryo; without it, the seed cannot germinate. Unhulled sunflower seed looks like the large grey-and-white striped seeds sold as bird food or snack food. Hulled sunflower kernels (the pale inner seed) have had the hull and embryo removed and cannot germinate.

Buying seed specifically for microgreen growing. For sunflower shoots, the key requirement is that the seed is unhulled and untreated — not heat-treated (as bird-food sunflower sometimes is) and not a hulled kernel. Microgreen seed suppliers stock sunflower seed in large packs specifically for tray growing.

content.text: For sunflower shoots, the most important purchasing decision is not which sunflower variety to choose but which form of the seed to buy. All large common sunflower varieties (the striped-seeded types used for oil, snacks, and bird food) produce good microgreen shoots. The variety is less important than the form.

is the required form for microgreen growing. The seed must have the outer black-and-grey-striped hull intact. This form looks like the large striped seeds in bird food mixes or in unshelled sunflower snack packs.

Hulled sunflower kernels (the pale cream inner seeds sold for baking, eating, or as a salad topping) do not germinate. The hull removal process removes the embryo. Do not use kernels for microgreen growing.

Some bird food sunflower seed is heat-treated to extend shelf life and prevent mould in outdoor feeders. Heat-treated seed has very low or zero viability for germination. Bird food from large outdoor retailers is a common source of non-viable sunflower seed for microgreen growers.

To avoid this problem, buy from a microgreen seed supplier, a sprouting seed supplier, or a health food store that sells raw unhulled sunflower seed for sprouting. These sources specifically stock unprocessed seed with full viability.
Variety differences at the microgreen stage

All common sunflower varieties with striped seeds produce the same microgreen shoots. This covers giant, multi-stem, and snack types. Only ornamental varieties with very small or dark seeds behave differently.
Ornamental varieties with small or dark seeds are less reliable. The best choice is large striped sunflower seed, sold for snacks or oil.

: buy unhulled sunflower seed from a microgreen seed supplier, a sprouting seed specialist, or a health food shop that stocks raw unhulled sunflower seed. Confirm the seed is labelled as untreated or for growing/sprouting. Quantities for regular tray growing: 500 g provides approximately 3 to 4 trays; 1 kg is a useful starting bulk for regular growers.
